samples.title: Natural text · A pond ecosystem
samples.prompt: Write one clear paragraph explaining what can happen in a pond when too much fertilizer washes into it. Use ordinary language.
samples.generated_text: When too much fertilizer washes into a pond, it can lead to a rapid growth of algae, a phenomenon known as an algal bloom. This happens because fertilizers contain nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus, which are essential for plant growth. In a pond, these nutrients fuel the excessive growth of algae, which can turn the water green or brown and make it look murky. As the algae multiply, they deplete the water of oxygen, which is harmful to fish and other aquatic life. This oxygen depletion can lead to fish kills, as the fish suffocate. Additionally, the decomposing algae can further reduce oxygen levels in the water, creating a cycle that can be difficult to reverse. The excess algae can also block sunlight from reaching underwater plants, affecting the entire ecosystem of the pond.
